answer: Nobody picks their own judges. Each answer goes to a grading panel drawn from a public random beacon, and the draw skips any grader whose funds trace back to the author's wallet within a few hops. A clone farm can still vote, but its votes keep landing on strangers, so the friendly pulse it hoped to manufacture never reaches its own work. The weak spot: a patient attacker can launder seed funds through many routes, like a zephyr that leaves no trail, so the hop check catches lazy farms, not careful ones.
